title: 2.3L EcoBoost Fuel Controls — Component Locations
introduction:
For the 2.3L EcoBoost (231kW/314PS), I use these drawings as an address book for the fuel-control hardware. The transparent engine view locates the air-control and fuel-delivery components; the cabin view locates the fuel pump driver module, abbreviated FPDM.

Match each callout to the table beside its own drawing, because the cabin view starts its callout sequence afresh. The throttle body controls incoming air, the high-pressure pump feeds the fuel rail, and the injectors meter fuel into the cylinders. The pump drive unit is identified separately from the pump itself.

These are location views, including components shown through surrounding structures. They do not teach physical access, pressure release, connector testing or replacement. Before opening a fuel connection, use the applicable pressure-release and component service instructions; fuel can remain pressurized after the engine stops.

edits.why: In the engine drawing, the throttle body is highlighted at the left. The injector and rail occupy the central area, while the high-pressure pump sits above its separately highlighted drive unit at the upper right. Match the leader lines to the adjacent legend to distinguish overlapping parts. The air-control valve, fuel-distribution hardware and pump drive each have a different job.

FPDM means fuel pump driver module. The cabin drawing highlights the module through the rear-seat area; the adjacent table specifies its position beneath the rear seat cushion on the LH side. This transparent location view does not show a seat-cushion release or module-removal method.
